# The Workstation's tooltips arrive in the stock blue, not its own palette

## Context

#18071 / PR #18072 gave the dock header actions tooltips, so `apps/workstation` renders Neo tooltips for the first time. It renders them in the stock theme blue.

**Measured** (dev server, `apps/workstation`, `dev@fabb61f001`, dark theme): a `.neo-tooltip` element rendered against the live tokens computes `background rgb(62, 99, 221)` — `#3E63DD`, declared as `--tooltip-bg` in `resources/scss/theme-neo-light/tooltip/Base.scss` and reached through the neo-dark theme's own value — with `color rgb(255,255,255)`, `border none`, `box-shadow none`, `border-radius 4px`. The app's chrome around it is `--workstation-ground #0b0e13`, `--workstation-panel #141a23`, `--workstation-signal #5eead4` (teal). Operator-reported from the running app.

The Workstation is its own theme authority — `theme-neo-{dark,light}/apps/workstation/Viewport.scss` open with *"App-owned palette: Workstation is its own theme authority"* — so a stock-blue overlay is the one piece of chrome that does not belong to it.

## The Problem

Nothing is broken; a surface the app never consumed before is now visible and unclaimed. The Workstation already answers this exact question for every other reused engine surface: it projects its palette into the engine's token slots rather than re-declaring rules. `--agent-dock-preview-*`, `--agent-dock-proxy-border` and the dock rail/reveal families are all filled that way. Tooltips are simply the newest member of that set and have no projection yet.

The scope matters and is the one non-obvious part. `Neo.tooltip.Base.createSingleton` builds one shared instance per app with `componentId: app.mainView.id`, and the node is created lazily on first target-over — it does **not** live inside `.workstation-workspace`. So a projection scoped to the workspace would never reach it. The themed root in this app is `BODY.neo-theme-neo-dark`, which is why the palette belongs at the `:root .neo-theme-neo-*` scope the app's Viewport theme files already use.

## The Architectural Reality

- `resources/scss/src/tooltip/Base.scss` — the whole rule is eight tokens: `--tooltip-bg`, `--tooltip-border`, `--tooltip-borderradius`, `--tooltip-boxshadow`, `--tooltip-color`, `--tooltip-fontsize`, `--tooltip-height`, `--tooltip-padding`. No rule to re-declare; the surface is already consumer-skinnable.
- `resources/scss/theme-neo-{dark,light}/tooltip/Base.scss` — the theme defaults, including the `#3E63DD` this ticket is about.
- `resources/scss/theme-neo-{dark,light}/apps/workstation/Viewport.scss` — the app's palette and its existing projections, at `:root .neo-theme-neo-*`. Loaded only when the Workstation Viewport class instantiates, so the scope is broad but the file is not.
- `resources/scss/src/apps/workstation/Workspace.scss:98-105` — the reveal overlay's projection, which is the grammar this should match: a surface token, a signal-tinted border, a ground-based elevation.

## The Fix

Add a `--tooltip-*` projection block to both `theme-neo-dark/apps/workstation/Viewport.scss` and `theme-neo-light/apps/workstation/Viewport.scss`, beside the existing `--agent-dock-preview-*` projections, reading only the app's own palette variables. Values follow the reveal overlay's grammar so the tooltip reads as a member of the same family: a signal-tinted elevated surface, a signal-tinted border against the app's line colour, app ink, and an elevation appropriate to each theme's ground.

Structure is untouched: no rule is re-declared, `--tooltip-height` and `--tooltip-padding` stay with the engine, and every other consumer renders byte-identically because the file only loads with the Workstation Viewport.

### Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--tooltip-{bg,color,border,boxshadow}` under the Workstation | `src/tooltip/Base.scss` (the eight-token rule); the app's own `body:has()` bridges for floating direct-body chrome | resolve from the Workstation palette in both themes, declared on the tooltip element itself (amended 2026-09-02 — see AC-3; the `:root .neo-theme-neo-*` shape ties with the theme sheet and loses on load order) | an app that does not load the Workstation Viewport keeps the theme defaults untouched | comment beside the block naming why the scope is the theme root and not the workspace | a rendered `.neo-tooltip` computes the app's values in both themes; the stock blue appears in neither |

**Decision Record impact:** `none` — a consumer filling engine token slots is the documented path, not a deviation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 In `apps/workstation`, neo-dark: a rendered `.neo-tooltip` computes a background derived from the Workstation palette, ink-coloured text, a signal-tinted border and a visible elevation — and **not** `rgb(62,99,221)`.
- [ ] AC-2 Same in neo-light, from that theme's own palette; the two are independently derived, not one value reused.
- [ ] AC-3 A tooltip mounted outside the workspace subtree resolves the app's values. **Amended 2026-09-02 on the reviewer's ask:** the prescription below said "at the theme root"; the shipped scope is the ELEMENT (`body:has(.workstation-viewport) .neo-tooltip`). The theme-root shape was implemented first and measured as a complete no-op — the tooltip theme sheet declares at that same `:root .neo-theme-*` weight and loads later, so a theme-root projection ties and loses on order. Naming the element also lets the projection follow the singleton's own runtime theme stamp, which a body-inherited one cannot.
- [ ] AC-4 No rule in `src/tooltip/Base.scss` is re-declared and no engine default changes; an app that does not load the Workstation Viewport renders byte-identically.
- [ ] AC-5 Read by eye in the running app in both themes, since the acceptance here is visual.

## Out of Scope

- A `--tooltip-fontfamily` token. The engine's rule has no font-family slot, so matching the app's mono voice would need an engine addition (the precedent exists — `--dock-rail-tab-font-family`), and re-declaring `font-family` app-side is exactly the re-declaration this ticket avoids. Worth its own leaf if the sans voice reads wrong.
- Every other consumer's tooltips, and the engine's own theme defaults.
- `--tooltip-height` / `--tooltip-padding`: structure, not identity.

## Avoided Traps

- **Scoping the projection to `.workstation-workspace`.** The shared tooltip is not a descendant of it; the projection would silently never apply, and the symptom would read as "the tokens do not work" rather than "the scope is wrong".
- **Re-declaring `.neo-tooltip` in app SCSS.** The engine comment on the rail tabs already names this trap: an app rule in an equal-specificity tie with the engine's, won on load order.
- **Reusing one colour for both themes.** The app's light and dark palettes are independently authored; a shared literal would drift from whichever one moves first.

## Related

`#18071` / PR `#18072` (which made tooltips visible here) · `#17633` (rail paint tokens — the same promote-to-token pattern) · `#17614` · `#18036` (the DockLayouts styling guide slot, where this belongs once written)

- 2026-09-02T14:48:11Z @neo-opus-ada referenced in commit `7c248d6` - "docs(workstation): the tooltip bridge names the weight that actually decides it (#18096)

The comment claimed the app's theme-root projections "work only because
nothing else declares them". They do not: the dock values layer declares its
defaults at `:where(.neo-theme-*)`, which carries zero specificity, so those
projections win on weight. The tooltip theme sheet declares at `:root
.neo-theme-*` — the same (0,2,0) a theme-root projection would use — so there
the projection only ties and loses on load order. Safe by design in one case,
not by absence in both.

Also records the second reason the scope has to be the element rather than an
ancestor: the shared singleton stamps the hovered target's theme onto itself,
so after the app's runtime toggle the tooltip carries `neo-theme-neo-light`
while `body` still carries `neo-theme-neo-dark`, and a body-inherited
projection could never follow that.

Both corrections are @neo-fable-clio's, from the PR #18098 review."
- 2026-09-02T14:50:46Z @neo-opus-ada referenced in commit `5558652` - "fix(workstation): tooltips join the app's floating chrome instead of arriving stock blue (#18096)

The dock header actions gained tooltips, so the shared singleton now paints in
this app for the first time — in the stock theme blue, the one piece of chrome
not speaking the Workstation's palette.

It joins the overflow menu's bridge and deliberately reuses its values: a
tooltip and that menu are both transient label chrome and should not disagree
about what floating chrome looks like here. The palette tokens differ per
theme, so one block serves both.

The `body:has()` scope is load-bearing rather than stylistic. The theme ships
`:root .neo-theme-neo-* { --tooltip-bg: … }` at (0,2,0), and
`theme-neo-*/tooltip/Base.css` is appended after this app's sheets — so a
projection written at that same weight, the shape the `--agent-dock-preview-*`
block uses, loses the tie on load order. Those projections work only because
nothing else declares them. Naming the floating element reaches (0,2,1) and
sets the tokens on the node that reads them, so no ancestor has to be guessed:
the tooltip is one lazily created instance bound to the main view, never a
workspace descendant."
